annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, fixed stable-product algorithm, operational error family, and uniform first-order interpretation of equation (8)

assumptions: The matrix dimension is positive and the exact and computed operands are real square n-by-n matrices, as in equation (1) and the recursive-inversion application of equation (8).
One otherwise unspecified matrix norm is used throughout and satisfies nonnegativity, definiteness, homogeneity, subadditivity, and submultiplicativity.
One multiplication operation, norm family, and nonnegative function mu are fixed across dimensions, inputs, calls, and positive precisions; mu has one global polynomial-growth certificate.
The exact operands are fixed while their computed perturbations and inherited absolute-error bounds vary with epsilon; both inherited errors are uniformly O(epsilon) on one positive radius.

Every computed output is the actual result of the fixed multiplication operation on the two perturbed operands, and its local error satisfies equation (1) with one uniform epsilon-squared coefficient.

The conclusion bounds the full realized product error without subtracting the inherited cross product or any local remainder; no exceptional-value semantics are added beyond the paper's real-valued normwise model.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P10 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P10 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p10_t2_first_order_product_error {n : Nat} (algorithm : P10StableMatrixMultiplication) (family : P10FirstOrderProductFamily algorithm n) : exists secondOrderCoeff : Real, 0 <= secondOrderCoeff and exists radius : Real, 0 < radius and forall epsilon : P10PositiveEpsilon, (epsilon : Real) <= radius -> (algorithm.matrixNorm n).value (p10ProductFamilyError algorithm family epsilon) <= p10ProductFamilyErrorBudget algorithm family epsilon + secondOrderCoeff * (epsilon : Real)^2
formal_statement.plain_language: For one fixed stable matrix-multiplication algorithm and one uniformly first-order family of inherited operand errors, the actual absolute normwise product error is bounded by equation (8)'s three leading terms plus one uniform quadratic remainder.

informal_proof: Expand the actual error as localError + A*dB + dA*B + dA*dB. Apply subadditivity, submultiplicativity, the local equation-(1) certificate, and the two inherited-error bounds. Their uniform O(epsilon) certificates bound dA*dB by leftCoeff*rightCoeff*epsilon^2; add this coefficient to the local quadratic coefficient.
informal_statement: Equation (8)'s complete three-term first-order absolute normwise product-error rule for the actual output of one fixed multiplication algorithm, with every suppressed effect bounded by one explicit uniform O(epsilon^2) term.
paper_version: published journal version; volume 108, 2007, printed pages 59-91

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: All 24 compiled modules in metadata/library_olean.json were searched. tier_rationale: The proof combines the local stable-multiplication certificate, both uniform inherited-error certificates, three abstract submultiplicative bounds, and repeated subadditivity after a paper-specific four-term expansion of the actual error. The L proof materially combines NumStability.matMul_add_left and NumStability.matMul_add_right from the frozen MatrixAlgebra module to derive that expansion. Searches across all 24 mounted modules found no declaration giving equation (8)'s linked uniform bound; the closer source-only MatMulFirstOrderSpec is not mounted, while the mounted Frobenius and entrywise results would improperly change the source's unnamed norm semantics.
